name: Thomas Rousseau
description: American Patriot Front leader assessed through his public national programme and organisational practice, with economic-policy gaps explicitly identified.

religion.reason: The reviewed sources describe Christian group symbolism but do not firmly establish Rousseau’s own personal religious identification.

sources.title: Interview with Thomas Rousseau
sources.publisher: VoxNR, nationalist advocacy publisher; interview is primary self-description

axes.brief: His proposed racial republic restricts citizenship and rejects dependence on ordinary electoral politics.
axes.counterEvidence: Consent rhetoric is counter-evidence; it does not establish universal equal suffrage.

axes.brief: National discipline constrains dissent, while he claims protections against the existing state.
axes.counterEvidence: Criticism of current policing is not a commitment to equal liberty under his proposed order.

axes.brief: Ancestry defines national membership, excluding equal plural citizenship.
axes.counterEvidence: Cultural training matters internally but does not remove the stated racial boundary.

qualifications.15: The statement specifically includes several distinct ways of life within national identity; it does not ask whether a common national identity should exist.

axes.brief: Ending foreign settlement and repatriation are stated objectives.
axes.counterEvidence: Limited European assimilation differs from general openness; individual visa instruments remain inferred.

qualifications.5: The statement permits permanent refugee settlement regardless of skills or cultural compatibility. The answer concerns this unconditional clause, separately from selected humanitarian admissions.

axes.brief: He opposes overseas wars while valuing national defence and martial strength.
axes.counterEvidence: Internal intimidation and physical training contradict general pacifism.

axes.brief: National sovereignty limits foreign political authority.
axes.counterEvidence: Solidarity with European nationalists does not establish shared international jurisdiction.

axes.brief: The programme favours national control without specifying universal public ownership.
axes.counterEvidence: Praise for industrialists and workers does not supply a sector-by-sector economic plan.

axes.brief: Domestic national capacity takes precedence over unqualified foreign economic access.
axes.counterEvidence: Detailed tariffs are not documented; shared European ancestry does not imply a free-trade treaty.

axes.brief: Private initiative likely operates within national strategic direction.
axes.counterEvidence: No complete planning or monetary programme is established; estimates have low confidence.

axes.brief: Material support for national insiders coexists with property and merit language.
axes.counterEvidence: Charitable activities are not proof of universal redistributive entitlements.

axes.brief: Christian cultural identity can coexist with political primacy over clergy.
axes.counterEvidence: Neither a clerical veto nor personal faith is firmly established.

axes.brief: He explicitly favours conventional families and opposes homosexuality and gender change.
axes.counterEvidence: Selective community activism does not establish equal civil treatment of opposing identities.

axes.brief: Practical tools serve national renewal under social safeguards.
axes.counterEvidence: Digital campaigning is not a biomedical permission programme; detailed technology choices remain weak analogies.

qualifications.13: No embryo-enhancement proposal is established. Traditional family and aversion to transforming youth make caution more likely than inferring permission from ancestry politics.

axes.brief: A unified racial national state constrains autonomous political communities.
axes.counterEvidence: Regional organisational networks are not a constitutional federalism policy.

axes.brief: Inherited racial membership coexists with deliberate cultural training.
axes.counterEvidence: Race doctrine does not document his causal answer for each temperament or intelligence mechanism.
